chunks: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man made a bequest to two men. Is it permissible for one of them to take half the inheritance alone, and the other the other half? He replied: It is not fitting for them to contradict the deceased, and they should act according to what he commanded them, if God wills.
2. Ali ibn al-Hasan, from his two brothers Muhammad and Ahmad, from their father, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazeed, from Burayd ibn Muawiya, who said:

A man died and made a bequest to me and to another, or to two men. One of them said: Take half of what he left and give me the half of what he left. The other refused. They asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, and he said: That is for him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh (may God have mercy on him) mentioned that he does not act upon this report nor issue fatwa based on it, but rather acts upon the first report, presuming them to be contradictory. However, the matter is not as he presumed, because his saying 'That is for him' does not explicitly mean that for the one who sought exclusive possession of half the inheritance. It is not impossible that what is meant by 'That is for him' is the one who refused to submit to his partner's desire. Thus, the summary is that he has the right to refuse him and not answer his question. On this basis, there is no contradiction between them in any case.
3. As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt owed to him by another man, who then died, leaving two executors. Is it permissible for the debt to be paid to one of the executors without the other? He said: It is not proper unless the ruler has divided the money, placing half in the hand of this one and half in the hand of that one, or they both come together by the order of the ruler. The explanation of this report is that if the just ruler divided it, it is permissible; and if the unjust ruler, it is permissible for him to manage it due to a type of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah).
ai.seo_question: Can one executor claim half the inheritance exclusively when there are two executors appointed by the deceased?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi presents a nuanced jurisprudential analysis in Chapter 69, reconciling apparent contradictions between reports regarding the authority of dual executors (wasiyyan) over an estate. The text clarifies that unilateral claims are valid unless contested, and highlights the role of the just ruler (al-sultan al-adl) in dividing assets or the principle of taqiyyah in cases of unjust authority, reflecting key Shia legal methodologies. This discussion underscores the importance of joint consent in estate management to prevent conflict among executors.
